pumac-2014-finals-a-01.prompt: Let $\gamma$ be the incircle of $\triangle ABC$ (i.e. the circle inscribed in $\triangle ABC$) for which $AB+AC=3BC$. Let the point where $AC$ is tangent to $\gamma$ be $D$. Let the incenter be $I$. Let the intersection of the circumcircle of $\triangle BCI$ with $\gamma$ that is closer to $B$ be $P$. Show that $P$, $I$, $D$ are collinear.
pumac-2014-finals-a-01.answer: $P$ is the antipode of $D$ on $\gamma$; this follows from $AI=2\,LI$ where $L$ is the centre of circle $BCI$.

pumac-2014-finals-a-03.prompt: There are $n$ coins lying in a circle. Each coin has two sides, $+$ and $-$. A *flop* means to flip every coin that has two different neighbours simultaneously, while leaving the others alone. For instance, $++-+$, after one flop, becomes $+---$. For $n$ coins, let us define $M$ to be a *perfect number* if for any initial arrangement of the coins, the arrangement of the coins after $M$ flops is exactly the same as the initial one. (a) When $n=1024$, find a perfect number $M$. (b) Find all $n$ for which a perfect number $M$ exists.
pumac-2014-finals-a-03.answer: (a) $M=512$ works (and every multiple of $512$). (b) A perfect number exists exactly when $3\nmid n$.
